correctness.rationale: A graph face is encoded exactly as a partial orientation with tail outdegree at most one and no directed cycle; this is equivalent to an acyclic Hasse matching. The package enumerates every legal face recursively and separately checks all \(3^{12}\) raw edge states. It verifies the full face vector, every codimension-one face, \(\partial^2=0\), and exact mod-\(2\) boundary ranks by three elimination orientations. These give \(\widetilde\beta_5=4\), \(\widetilde\beta_6=139\), and zero otherwise, with an independent Euler check. Risk: the statement is coefficient-specific; nothing here proves the integral groups or full homotopy type.

value.rationale: The cube \(Q_3\) is the smallest hypercube beyond \(Q_2\), which is a cycle and lies in a previously computed family. Hypercubes are explicitly singled out in the checked connectivity literature, so the first new hypercube case is a natural calibration point rather than an arbitrary graph. The answer is structurally informative: reduced mod-\(2\) homology occurs in two adjacent dimensions, ruling out a single-dimensional wedge-of-spheres model, and it sharpens a general connectivity bound to complete mod-\(2\) homology for this first case. The exact finite computation therefore has motivated standalone value without claiming a general \(Q_n\) theorem.
